nodes.text: No merchant credit, refund, reversal, void, or adjustment offsets the disputed duplicate in DSP-2026-90004. TXN-C04-FIRST and TXN-C04-SECOND are the only transactions linked to ORD-C04; both are posted purchases of $64.18, and neither has a REFUNDS relationship or an adjustment/credit transaction. Therefore completed credit = $0.00, initiated-but-not-completed credit = $0.00, and the duplicate amount remains $64.18.

nodes.label: MemoryNote
nodes.text: Missing-evidence hygiene: the absence of supplied merchant evidence is not an unanswered evidence request. Apply a missing-evidence default only when the dispute has a REQUESTED relationship to an EvidenceRequest whose deadline passed without response; no REQUESTED edge means the procedural default is unavailable. Sources: DSP-2026-90004.

nodes.label: MemoryNote
nodes.text: Duplicate-amount reconciliation: absence of a refund, reversal, void, credit, or adjustment means the disputed amount remains unreduced, but it does not by itself prove duplicate processing. Assess duplicate status from authorization and clearing evidence separately from credit-offset status. Sources: TXN-C04-FIRST, TXN-C04-SECOND, DSP-2026-90004.

nodes.label: MemoryNote
nodes.text: Duplicate-processing review: when two posted transactions share one approved authorization, have explicit sequential clearing numbers, and their amounts reconcile to the authorization total, treat them as one authorization lifecycle (potential split capture), not an improper duplicate. An unusual posting gap alone is insufficient to establish a separate purchase or retry. Sources: TXN-C04-FIRST, TXN-C04-SECOND.
